solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drink little watery? No way!

parts.note: a little is a bit

indicators.note: 'No way!' tells us the letters of way are taken out of watery

parts.note: taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: Someone rejects a weak, watery drink in disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing W, A and Y from WATERY leaves TER.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter is a type of British ale, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Smallest price for car with silencer?

parts.note: the Mini is a small British car
'Mum's the word' is a call for silence, so mum is a silencer

explanation.surface: Asking what the cheapest price is for a car fitted with a silencer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'price for' is padding that joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The minimum is the least amount possible, the smallest quantity.

clue.text: Handcraft?

parts.note: read as hand (of cards) plus craft (skill): skill in playing a hand of cards

explanation.surface: Looks like a single word for manual craftwork.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word: a hand at cards and craft, meaning skill or know-how.
explanation.definitionFit: Good judgment in card play is skill at managing the hand you are dealt.

clue.text: On subject of fuel, nothing new

parts.note: re means concerning, on the subject of
peat is dug and burned as fuel

explanation.surface: A complaint that talk about fuel brings nothing fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerun or rebroadcast offers viewers nothing they have not already seen.

clue.text: Not on the rocks, as in job

parts.note: off is the opposite of on
a drink 'on the rocks' is served over ice

explanation.surface: Someone explains a drink is served neat, as they would at work.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a post or position of duty, a job someone holds.

clue.text: Heading in the right direction to get qualifications?

definitions.meaning: attending a course of study to earn a qualification

explanation.surface: Someone making good progress toward gaining qualifications.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means progressing as planned, and a student taking classes is literally attending a course.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on track toward a goal also describes enrolment in a programme of study.

clue.text: 'Trees' has T at the front

parts.note: firs are coniferous trees

explanation.surface: A note on spelling: the word trees begins with T.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming ahead of all others means leading, in the lead position.

clue.text: Sorry argument against: unoriginal

parts.note: the cons are the arguments against, as in pros and cons
trite means hackneyed, unoriginal

explanation.surface: An apology dismissed as a stale counter-argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling remorse for a wrong done is being penitent, truly regretful.

clue.text: Does like it when one has friends round

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: one and friends go around the word it, enclosing it

parts.note: mates are friends
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys it when they have friends over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' is a verb here, not the plural of doe; 'when' and 'has' are joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy or mimic someone is to behave just as they do.

clue.text: Heavens! Going in to perform for recording!

indicators.note: the exclamation is placed inside the verb for performing

parts.note: to sing is to perform vocally
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'heavens!' (as in 'cor blimey')

explanation.surface: An excited cry as someone goes into a studio to make a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'for' are joining words; 'recording' is the definition, not part of the surface's studio.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping the score means recording points as a game goes on.

clue.text: Bound to have had run-through: to have practised

indicators.note: the abbreviation for run goes through the middle of the word for bound

parts.note: bound means tied up
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to have had a rehearsal, so has practised.
explanation.definitionFit: A tried method is tested and proven by experience, like a practised one.

clue.text: Complete change of opinion regarding act

parts.note: about means regarding, concerning
a turn is a performer's act

explanation.surface: A total U-turn in someone's view of a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a military drill command to face the opposite way, it is used for a reversal of policy.

clue.text: Three-quarters meat diet for an insectivore

indicators.note: three of the four letters are kept, so the last one is dropped

parts.note: beef is meat

explanation.surface: A meal plan of mostly meat for a creature that eats insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Insect-eaters dine on insects, and this buzzing insect is one such meal.

clue.text: For which waster, a foreigner, entered casino?

definitions.text: For which waster, a foreigner, entered casino?

indicators.note: the foreigner goes into the word for waster

parts.note: a roué is a debauched rake, a waster
a Lett is a Latvian, a foreigner

explanation.surface: Asking what game a dissolute foreigner went into a casino to play.
explanation.walkthrough: A roué is an old word for a rake; a Lett is a Latvian. The whole clue also defines the game.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning-wheel gambling game is a casino staple that a rake might play.

clue.text: English cooks about to turn over puddings

indicators.note: the reversed cooks go around the English abbreviation
the word for cooks is turned backwards

parts.note: stews means cooks slowly

explanation.surface: English chefs are about to flip their desserts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn over' makes SWETS, and 'about' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage sweets are desserts served after the main course.

clue.text: As clue for 'rode', it's a bad 'un!

parts.note: the word doer rearranged makes rode, so that phrase clues it

explanation.surface: Pretends to judge a clue for the word rode as poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' is the anagram signal on DOER, giving RODE: the answer is the clue that produces it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad 'un is a villain, someone who commits offences.

clue.text: A tail's for wagging: an essential for a dog

indicators.note: the tail's letters are wagged about into a new order

parts.note: the letters of A TAILS, possessive S included
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wagging tail is essential to any dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for wagging' turns A TAILS into ALSATI; 'essential for a' is padding before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alsatian, or German shepherd, is a breed of dog.

clue.text: Forecast had been upset

indicators.note: in a down-clue sense, upset turns the word over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: was is a past form of be

explanation.surface: The weather forecast had been overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to see ahead, so having forecast something you saw it coming.

clue.text: Aren't getting stick in debate

indicators.note: the word for stick goes inside the contraction

parts.note: the letters of the contraction, apostrophe dropped
gum is glue, something that sticks

explanation.surface: Debaters aren't being criticised in the discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' is glue, not criticism; 'getting' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispute or reasoned discussion between opposing sides is a disagreement or debate.

clue.text: The female's a man, right?

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether the woman is really a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The objective pronoun refers to a woman or girl already mentioned.

clue.text: C-Casanova found hiding in the grass?

parts.note: the stammered first letter C
Casanova was a famous lover

explanation.surface: A stammered report of a womaniser caught hiding in the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found hiding in the' is padding; the stutter supplies the extra C.
explanation.definitionFit: Clover is a low pasture plant grown with grasses as fodder, loosely called grass.

clue.text: Tending to be a little flat

definitions.meaning: inclined, likely, as in 'tending to forget'
a little way of writing flat, its abbreviation for apartment

explanation.surface: A flat that is somewhat small, inclined to be cramped.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inclined to do something matches the sense, and the abbreviation for apartment is a short form for flat.

clue.text: Snacks for the vegetable-crazy

parts.note: the pea is a vegetable
nuts means crazy

explanation.surface: Nibbles for people who are mad about vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundnuts sold salted in bags are a classic bar snack.

clue.text: With parent out more, it's easy

parts.note: pa is a short word for father
if you are out more, you are in less

explanation.surface: A parent going out more makes life easier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is a joining word; being out more means spending less time at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Something causing no hurt or effort is simple to get through.

clue.text: Lost arts making comeback? Yes, all round

indicators.note: the word for yes is placed around the reversed arts

parts.note: ay (aye) means yes

indicators.note: the word arts comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The lost arts are returning, and yes, everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' gives STRA, which 'all round' puts between A and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone off the right path, so missing or mislaid.

clue.text: Scatters bouquets

definitions.meaning: to spray is to scatter droplets
a spray is a bunch of cut flowers

explanation.surface: Someone flinging flower bunches about.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means disperses in droplets, and the noun is a bunch of flowers.

clue.text: Wasn't perfect — crust was too delicate

definitions.meaning: the earth's crust is cracked by geological faults

explanation.surface: A baker admits the pastry crust was too fragile.
explanation.walkthrough: The pastry crust is the false trail: geological faults are fractures in the earth's crust.
explanation.definitionFit: Having flaws means being imperfect, and a crust with fractures has faults.

clue.text: If I abandoned one instrument for another…

indicators.note: I is dropped from the word If

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the letter removed
the lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A musician considers swapping one instrument for another.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing I from IF leaves F; 'another' (instrument) is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodwind instrument is a different instrument from the stringed one in the wordplay.

clue.text: He gives party (spelled 'paty'?)

parts.note: a do is a party
party spelt as paty has no R

explanation.surface: A man throws a party and someone queries the spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who donates gifts or blood is a giver.

clue.text: Lengthens shorts

parts.note: shorts are spirits, and adding water or a mixer makes a long drink

explanation.walkthrough: Shorts are not trousers: they are small measures of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding water weakens a spirit and turns it into a longer drink.

clue.text: It's ornamental but fasteners are irritating

parts.note: tapes are ties used to fasten things
to try someone is to irritate them, as in 'try my patience'

explanation.surface: A decorative item spoiled by annoying fastenings.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven wall hanging is a decorative textile.

clue.text: Hell-bent on getting oxygen?

definitions.meaning: a patient given oxygen may be put inside an oxygen tent

explanation.surface: Someone determined to get oxygen at any cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Being resolved on a purpose is being determined; inside an oxygen tent is the punning second sense.
